crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Expense Fraud
children.blurb: Expense fraud covers claims that are false, inflated, duplicated or outside policy, from a fabricated taxi receipt to a supplier invoice routed through an employee's own account.

children.name: Money Laundering Networks
children.blurb: Money laundering networks are the webs of accounts, shell companies, intermediaries and counterparties used to move the proceeds of crime so their origin is obscured.

children.name: Phantom Vendors and Procurement Fraud
children.blurb: Phantom vendors and procurement fraud covers the creation of fake suppliers, shell companies, or inflated invoices that divert an organisation's money to an insider or an outside colluder.

children.name: Communication Forensics
children.blurb: Communication forensics is the examination of messages, calls, emails and documents to establish who said what, when, and whether the record can be trusted.

children.name: Tracing and Recovering Digital Assets
children.blurb: Tracing and recovering digital assets covers the work of following value as it moves through bank ledgers, card networks, payment processors, exchange accounts, wallets and internal accounting systems, then trying to get it back.

sections.body: Fraud detection and forensics applies artificial intelligence to finding financial misconduct, from fake expense claims to complex money laundering. In practice, models scan transaction logs, receipts, and vendor records for patterns that human reviewers would miss at scale. Expense fraud systems flag duplicate submissions, inflated categories, and unusual timing against an employee's own history. Money laundering networks are mapped by graph algorithms that trace flows across accounts and jurisdictions. Communication forensics uses natural language processing to review emails, chats, and documents for intent, collusion, or concealment. Digital asset tracing follows cryptocurrency movements through public ledgers and exchange records.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is mature in narrow, high volume tasks like expense anomaly detection and vendor duplicate matching, where labeled data exists and outcomes are measurable. It is far less settled in adversarial settings, because fraudsters adapt and models degrade without constant retraining. Money laundering detection remains hard because legitimate and illegitimate flows often look similar, and false positives burden compliance teams. Communication forensics is limited by encryption, data privacy rules, and the difficulty of proving intent from text alone. Digital asset tracing works well on public blockchains but stops at mixers, privacy coins, and off ramp exchanges with weak records. No system replaces human judgment, and every output is a lead, not a conclusion.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages here follow the money and the messages in sequence. Expense Fraud covers the smallest unit, employee claims, and the models that score them. Phantom Vendors and Procurement Fraud widens the view to fake suppliers and bid rigging inside an organization. Money Laundering Networks then scales up to cross border flows and the graph methods used to expose them. Communication Forensics turns to the evidence in language, showing how text and chat are reviewed for coordination or concealment. Tracing and Recovering Digital Assets closes the chain by following value onto blockchains and through exchanges. A reader can start with any page, but the set is designed to move from a single suspicious receipt to a network spanning jurisdictions.
